# Source vs out

- Edit game logic in `source/` (`.scene.dry`, `.qdisplay.dry`, `info.dry`).
- Do not edit `out/` — built by `npm run dendrynexus make-html`.
- Verify changes with a local build when behavior matters.

--- description: Mikasa Dendry / Dendrynexus cheat sheet (from source/ patterns) globs: source/**/*.dry alwaysApply: true --- # Mikasa Dendry cheat sheet Dendry (`.dry`) is compiled by [dendrynexus](https://github.com/aucchen/dendrynexus) into `out/`. Syntax below is inferred from this repo; confirm edge cases with `npm run dendrynexus make-html -- --pretty`. ## Layout | Path | Role | |------|------| | `source/scenes/**/*.scene.dry` | Scenes, cards, events, advisors | | `source/qdisplays/*.qdisplay.dry` | Qualities: numeric ranges → labels | | `source/info.dry` | Game title / author metadata | | `out/` | Generated HTML/JS — do not edit | ## Scene file anatomy ```dry title: My Scene new-page: true is-card: true card-image: img/foo.jpg tags: event, govt_affairs priority: 1 max-visits: 1 view-if: month = 3 and year = 2300 on-arrival: foo += 1; bar = 1 go-to: post_event if started = 1; main if started = 0 Prose and choices here. - @choice_a: Label shown to player - @choice_b - #event @choice_a title: Choice title (cards) subtitle: Shown under title choose-if: police_defund = 0 and police_reform < 2 available-if: police_investigated = 0 unavailable-subtitle: Why this is greyed out on-arrival: police_reform += 1 on-depart: defund = 0 Choice body text. [? if police_reform = 1: Conditional prose ?] ``` - **`@subscene`** — block starting with `@name`; choices use `- @name` or `- @name: visible label`. - **`#tag`** — include all scenes tagged with that name (e.g. `- #event`, `- #party_affairs` in decks). - **`=` heading** — section title in UI (`= Status`). - **`>` blockquote** — quoted flavor text in `root.scene.dry`. ## Common scene metadata | Key | Purpose | |-----|---------| | `title:` | Display name | | `new-page:` | Open as new page (`true` / `false`) | | `is-card:` | Playable card | | `is-pinned-card:` | Stays in hand (e.g. advance month, advisors) | | `is-hand:` / `is-deck:` | Main UI: hand vs deck | | `max-cards:` | Hand size | | `card-image:` | Card art path | | `set-bg:` | Background image | | `tags:` | Grouping for `#tag` includes and filters | | `priority:` | Event ordering (higher first) | | `max-visits:` | `1` = one-shot event/card setup | | `view-if:` / `view_if:` | When scene/card appears (both spellings exist in repo) | | `on-arrival:` | Run on enter — JS block `{! … !}` or `stat += 1; stat2 = 0` | | `on-depart:` | Run when leaving subscene | | `on-display:` | JS when scene renders (DOM / `fetch`, see `mod_loader.scene.dry`) | | `go-to:` | Auto-navigate: `scene`, `scene.subscene`, or conditions | ### `go-to` examples (from repo) ```dry go-to: post_event.events_choice go-to: main if difficulty >= 0; main.main_easy if difficulty < 0 go-to: organize_phase_tick.scene.dry go-to: events_choice if has_event = 1; main if has_event = 0 ``` ### Choice gating (subscenes) | Key | Purpose | |-----|---------| | `choose-if:` / `chose-if:` | Must be true to pick (typo `chose-if` appears in source) | | `available-if:` | Alternative gating style | | `unavailable-subtitle:` | Text when disabled; may embed `[? … ?]` | ## Inline templating | Syntax | Meaning | |--------|---------| | `[+ var +]` | Insert quality/stat value | | `[+ month : month +]` | Value with qdisplay label (see `month.qdisplay.dry`) | | `[? if x = 1: text ?]` | Conditional prose | | `[? if x => 1: text ?]` | Comparison in condition | | `{! JavaScript or HTML !}` | Execute JS or emit raw HTML | HTML tooltips and party colors are common: ```dry {!C!}:[+ Exec_C +] ``` Party letter colors: **C** corp `#44b88f`, **G** gang `#cf6e19`, **D** dem `#1100cc`, **H** hate `#3a0000ff`, **I** ind `#404040`. ## JavaScript blocks - Wrap logic in `{! … !}` (multiline OK). - **`Q`** — primary game state namespace (`Q.month`, `Q.update_projections()`, classes on `Q` in `root.scene.dry`). - Top-level assignments in `on-arrival` often omit `let`/`const` (Dendrynexus global scope). - **`on-arrival:` without braces** — semicolon-separated stat updates: `on-arrival: patriot_meme_strength += 1;` - Runtime APIs appear in advanced scenes: `this.game.scenes`, `this._compileChoices`, `this.ui` (`post_event.scene.dry`). ### Setup / tick pattern Hidden setup scenes (`max-visits: 1`, `new-page: false`) define functions and assign hooks: ```dry on-arrival: {! function organize_tick() { Q.protest_good += Q.non_violence - 1.5 } Q.monthly_tick_phase1 = monthly_tick_phase1 !} ``` Wire with `go-to:` from a visible card or `on-arrival` on phase start. ## Q-displays (`*.qdisplay.dry`) Map numeric qualities to text: ```dry (1..1) January (0.41..0.54) divided (..0.06) completely disloyal (0.95..) completely loyal ``` Used via `[+ month : month +]` — second name is the qdisplay id (usually filename stem). ## Game flow (this project) 1. **`root.scene.dry`** — init `Q` (stratums, regions, election math), start menu → `main` / `main_easy`. 2. **`main.scene.dry`** — decks: Party Affairs, Government Affairs, pinned shuffle/advance. 3. **`advance.scene.dry`** — month tick → `post_event`. 4. **`post_event.scene.dry`** — `Q.update_projections()`, drain `#event` queue or return to main. 5. **Events** — `tags: event`, `view-if:` date, `priority`, `max-visits: 1`. 6. **Cards** — `is-card: true`, `tags: organize_phase` / `govt_affairs` / `party_affairs`, often `view_if:` unlock flags. 7. **`status.scene.dry`**, **`library.scene.dry`**, **`election_simulation.scene.dry`** — `is-special: true`. 8. **`@backSpecialScene`** — return from special scenes (library, mods). ## Build ```bash npm install npm run dendrynexus make-html -- --pretty cp out/game.json out/html/ # if running static html locally ``` `--pretty` is passed through to dendrynexus (formatting/readability of generated output). ## Editing tips - Prefer matching existing spelling in the same file (`view-if` vs `view_if`, `choose-if` vs `chose-if`). - New events: copy a dated event (e.g. `september_convention.scene.dry`), set `view-if`, `tags: event`, add to event pool via `#event` if needed. - New qualities: add qdisplay file + reference in prose with `[+ name : qdisplay_id +]`. - Simulation / balance logic lives mainly in `root.scene.dry` and organizing ticks under `source/scenes/cards/organizing/`.

can you review the javascript code in root.scene.dry and suggest ways to clean it up?
</user_query>

Reading the full JavaScript in `root.scene.dry` for a structured review.

[REDACTED]

Here is a focused review of the JavaScript in the root `on-arrival` block (lines 4–353). I am not changing anything unless you ask — this is cleanup guidance only.

## Definite bugs (fix first)

**1. `region.appeals` getter is wrong**

```141:146:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
    get appeals() {
        let result = []
        for (var i = 0; i < Q.vote_labels.length; i++) {
            result.push(this.vote_labels)
        }
        return result
```

It pushes `this.vote_labels` (undefined) every time. It should match `stratum` / `interest`:

```javascript
result.push(this[Q.vote_labels[i]])
```

Right now `tabulate_region` uses `area.appeals`, so regional appeal shifts are effectively broken.

**2. `stratum_votes` uses bare `lookups`**

```237:238:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
    stratum_votes(stratum) {
        if (typeof (stratum) == 'string') { stratum = lookups[stratum] }
```

Should be `Q.lookups[stratum]` (as in `tabulate_region` and `interest_votes`). String lookups will fail or hit the wrong object.

**3. `UNAFFILIATED_LABEL` is set before `"Unaffiliated"` exists**

```61:63:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
Q.interest_labels = ["Executive", "Gold", "White", "Blue"]
Q.UNAFFILIATED_LABEL = Q.interest_labels[Q.interest_labels.length - 1]
Q.interest_labels.push(Q.UNAFFILIATED_LABEL) //might cause problems if this isn't last
```

That sets `UNAFFILIATED_LABEL` to `"Blue"` and duplicates `"Blue"` in the label list. Later you create `interest("Unaffiliated", ...)`. Likely intent:

```javascript
Q.interest_labels.push("Unaffiliated")
Q.UNAFFILIATED_LABEL = "Unaffiliated"
```

**4. Possible double-apply of `size` in `tabulate_region`**

```211:212:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
                let result = find_balance(appeals).map((x) => x * size)
                let product = result.map(x => x * size * 10000)
```

Votes are scaled by `size` twice (then ×10000). If that is not deliberate, use one scale step, e.g. `find_balance(appeals).map(x => x * size * 10000)`.

---

## Structural cleanup (biggest maintainability wins)

**1. Split “library” from “bootstrap”**

The block mixes four concerns:

| Concern | Lines (approx.) | Suggestion |
|--------|------------------|------------|
| Math helpers | 6–56 | `electionMath` object or plain functions |
| Domain classes | 77–302 | `Stratum`, `Region`, `Interest`, `Electorate` |
| World data | `setup_demographics` | Data-only tables |
| One-time init | 345–351 | Short init at bottom |

Even within one `{! !}` block, grouping with comments or an IIFE keeps Dendrynexus happy but reads clearer:

```javascript
(function initElectionModel() {
  // helpers, classes, setup_demographics, assign to Q
})()
```

**2. Replace constructor “assignment arguments”**

```309:309:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
    new stratum("rich", appeals = [0, 0, 0, 6, 1, 0, 2])
```

`appeals = [...]` assigns a global `appeals` and passes the array. Prefer normal arguments:

```javascript
new stratum("rich", [0, 0, 0, 6, 1, 0, 2])
```

Same for `populations =`, `memberships =`, etc.

**3. Centralize label-driven indices**

`drone_disenfranchise` hard-codes indices `2` and `6` (Corp / Apathy). Build once:

```javascript
Q.voteIndex = Object.fromEntries(Q.vote_labels.map((l, i) => [l, i]))
// then Q.voteIndex.Corp, Q.voteIndex.Apathy
```

Same for party seat mapping in `seat_projections` (`D`, `I`, `C`, …) — a small `PARTY_KEYS = ['D','I','C','G','H']` loop avoids five copy-pasted assignments per region.

**4. Deduplicate class boilerplate**

`stratum`, `region`, and `interest` all:

- copy `vote_labels` onto `this`
- register in `Q.lookups` / arrays
- expose nearly identical `appeals` getters

A shared helper reduces drift (which already produced the `region.appeals` bug):

```javascript
function applyVoteAppeals(target, appeals) {
  Q.vote_labels.forEach((label, i) => { target[label] = appeals[i] || 0 })
}
function registerLookup(collection, obj, name) {
  collection.push(obj)
  Q.lookups[name] = obj
}
```

**5. `electorate` constructor ignores its parameter**

```192:194:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
    constructor(global_shifts) {
        this.global_shifts = Q.global_shifts || [0, -20, 0, -1, -3, 0, 0]
```

Either use `global_shifts` or drop the parameter.

---

## Smaller code-quality fixes

**Implicit globals** — `results`, `i`, `converted`, `blank`, `polling`, `region`, etc. leak to Dendrynexus global scope. That may be required, but inside helpers use `let`/`const` and only attach APIs you need on `Q` (`Q.electorate`, `Q.update_projections`, …).

**`logistic_convert_list` call** — `logistic_convert_list(u = i, s = e, ...args)` uses assignment expressions as arguments. Prefer `logistic_convert_list(i, e, ...args)`.

**`piecewise_sub`** — unlike `piecewise_add` / `piecewise_mult`, it does not coerce missing values; `undefined - undefined` → `NaN` in seat math.

**`find_balance`** — returns `converted` after the loop; if the loop never runs meaningfully, `converted` can be undefined on first use. Initialize before the loop or return explicitly.

**`assign_percentages`** — guard `total_votes === 0` or `n_seats === 0` to avoid `NaN` remainders.

**`update_memberships`** — `ig[this.name] / this.size` will divide by zero if a stratum has no population.

**Naming** — PascalCase for classes (`Stratum`, `Electorate`) matches JS convention; lowercase works but is easy to confuse with instances.

**Magic numbers** — document or name constants:

```javascript
const EXEC_SEATS = 150
const GUILD_SEATS = 35
const DISTRICT_SEATS = 15
const VOTE_SCALE = 10000
```

---

## Performance (only if projections feel slow)

`Q.update_projections` → `seat_projections()` → `tabulate_global()` recomputes everything every time. For a monthly turn game that may be fine. If it gets slow:

- Cache last appeals hash and skip full tabulation when only a few stats changed
- Or split “full recount” vs “incremental update”

Not urgent unless you profile a problem.

---

## Dendry-specific constraint

All of this must stay inside `{! !}` (or whatever dendrynexus supports for external scripts). If the compiler allows a single external `.js` file included at build time, moving ~300 lines out of `root.scene.dry` would be the largest readability win; if not, the IIFE + sections approach above is the practical option.

---

## Suggested cleanup order

1. Fix `region.appeals`, `lookups` → `Q.lookups`, and `UNAFFILIATED_LABEL` / label list.
2. Confirm whether the double `size` multiply is intentional; fix if not.
3. Normalize constructor calls and add `let`/`const` in helpers.
4. Extract `setup_demographics` data into plain arrays/objects.
5. Refactor repeated seat-assignment and appeal-copy logic.

I can turn this into a concrete patch (minimal bugfixes only, or a fuller refactor) if you want to proceed in the repo.

[REDACTED]

Designing `root_new.scene.dry` with a VoterBlock-centric model. Checking how the current election API is consumed across the project.

[REDACTED]

Implementing `root_new.scene.dry` with a VoterBlock-centric model, preserving the existing `Q` API for compatibility.

[REDACTED]

Fixing stratum aggregation: it must sum per-region stratum totals (after drone disenfranchisement), not raw block votes.

[REDACTED]

Created `source/scenes/root_new.scene.dry` — a parallel root scene with the same menus and `Q` surface API, but a **VoterBlock-first** class layout.

## What changed structurally

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph atoms [Atomic layer]
        VB[VoterBlock]
    end
    subgraph dimensions [Dimensions]
        D[Demographic]
        A[Area]
        I[InterestGroup]
    end
    EM[ElectionModel facade]
    Q[(Q qualities)]

    D --> VB
    A --> VB
    I --> VB
    EM --> VB
    EM --> Q
```

| Class | Role |
|--------|------|
| **VoterBlock** | One cell: demographic × district × guild affiliation; `tabulate()` produces ideology vote vector |
| **Demographic** | Stratum (rich, first, …); `forEachBlock()` / `blocks()`; appeal edits via `Q.first["Dems"]` still work |
| **Area** | District (Docks, …); population per stratum; `Q.Docks` exposed |
| **InterestGroup** | Executive, Gold, …, Unaffiliated |
| **ElectionModel** | Builds blocks, tabulates, `seat_projections()` / `assign_seats()` |

**Ideology vs affiliation:** In your game data, **interest groups** are on the block (Executive, Blue, …). **Ideology** (Dems, Corp, Gang, …) is the *output* of the logistic split — not a third dimension on the block. Events that do `Q.first["Dems"] += 0.2` still target the demographic’s appeal vector.

## Patterns (why this shape)

1. **Composite / value object** — `VoterBlock` is the smallest unit you simulate; everything else is grouping or metadata.
2. **Bidirectional indexing** — Each dimension keeps `_blocks[]`; you can walk “all first-wave voters” or “all Docks voters” without nested loops over the full cube.
3. **Registry (`Q.lookups`)** — String names resolve to entities for legacy scenes and `tabulate_region("Docks")`.
4. **Facade (`ElectionModel`)** — Orchestration stays in one place; dimensions stay dumb about seat math.
5. **Factory + rebuild** — `rebuildBlocks()` materializes the full grid after data load (call again if you change populations/memberships structurally).
6. **IIFE** — Wraps init so helpers don’t leak globals (unlike the old root block).

## Compatibility kept

- `Q.electorate`, `Q.update_projections`, `Q.qified_pops()`
- `Q.stratums`, `Q.regions`, `Q.interests`, `Q.lookups`, label arrays
- `Q.rich`, `Q.first`, … and `Q.Docks`, …
- `assign_seats()` alias (for `election_simulation.scene.dry`)
- Legacy `size² × 10000` scaling so numbers stay comparable until you choose to fix balance

## Fixes baked in (vs old root)

- `UNAFFILIATED_LABEL` is actually `"Unaffiliated"`
- Area appeals use real values (old `region.appeals` bug)
- `stratum_votes` uses post–drone-disenfranchisement regional totals

## How to try it

Dendrynexus must load `root_new` instead of `root` (rename/swap, or change whatever scene is the game entry). Until then the game still uses `root.scene.dry`.

When you’re ready to compare projections side-by-side, we can add a small debug scene that prints `Exec_D`, `Docks_C`, etc. from both models.

## Next steps (when you’re satisfied)

1. Run `npm run dendrynexus make-html -- --pretty` and spot-check election/status screens.
2. Rename `root.scene.dry` → `root_legacy.scene.dry` and `root_new.scene.dry` → `root.scene.dry`.
3. Optionally drop the legacy `size²` multiplier once you accept new balance numbers.

If you want, I can add a `@debug_election_compare` subscene that logs key seat totals from both implementations before you swap.

Added a standalone Node path that mocks `Q` and runs the same election pipeline as the game.

## Usage

```bash
npm run simulate-election
# or
node scripts/simulate-election.js
node scripts/simulate-election.js --json
```

Default output mirrors the in-game election screen (executive, guilds, population table, districts). `--json` gives a structured snapshot for scripts or diffs.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `source/lib/election-model.js` | Voter-block model; `initElectionModel(Q)`, `formatElectionReport(Q)`, `electionSnapshot(Q)` |
| `scripts/simulate-election.js` | CLI: creates `Q`, runs `assign_seats()` + `qified_pops()`, prints results |

No Dendrynexus, no HTML build — only Node.

## API for other scripts

```javascript
const { initElectionModel, formatElectionReport } = require('./source/lib/election-model.js')

const { Q, model } = initElectionModel()

// Tweak appeals like event scenes do, then re-project:
Q.first['Dems'] += 0.3
Q.update_projections()

console.log(formatElectionReport(Q))
```

## Sync note

The logic lives in `source/lib/election-model.js`. `root_new.scene.dry` still has the inline `{! !}` copy for Dendry; there’s a comment pointing at the lib file. When you change the model, update both (or we can later wire a small sync script).

Party letters in output: **D** Dems, **I** Ind, **C** Corp, **G** Gang, **H** Hate (first five vote dimensions used for seats).

You’re right that the current stack mixes too many ideas in one logistic loop. A rebuild is reasonable if you treat it as a **pipeline with explicit stages**, not one formula per “voter block.”

## What you’re really modeling

Three separate questions get conflated today:

| Question | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Who can vote in this chamber?** | Guild seats ≈ guild members; district seats ≈ residents; executive ≈ wealth-weighted oligarchy |
| **Who actually turns out?** | Guild high; masses low until “awakening”; gangs spike when turnout is low |
| **How are preferences turned into seats?** | PR within each chamber; fringe vs mainstream sensitivity |

Answer each in its own module. `VoterBlock` (demographic × district × affiliation) is still a good atom for **population and local modifiers**; chambers and turnout sit above it.

## Recommended architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph state [Game state on Q]
        VB[Voter blocks]
        EV[Event modifiers]
        CAL[Election calendar]
    end

    subgraph pipe [Each election tick]
        A[1. Eligible electorate per chamber]
        B[2. Turnout per block]
        C[3. Party support / ideology]
        D[4. Effective votes]
        E[5. PR seat allocation]
        F[6. Write seats to Q]
    end

    VB --> A
    EV --> B
    EV --> C
    CAL --> A
    A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F
```

### 1. Chamber definitions (constants, not code soup)

Define each power center once:

```javascript
// example shape — tune numbers to your lore
const CHAMBERS = {
  executive: { seats: 150, weight: 'oligarch', elects: 'global' },
  guild:     { seats: 35,  perGuild: true, elects: 'global' }, // Gold/White/Blue
  district:  { seats: 15,  perDistrict: true, elects: 'rolling' },
}
```

- **Executive**: aggregate with wealth/skew (rich strata count more).
- **Guild**: only blocks (or population) tied to that guild; high base turnout.
- **District**: all residents in that district; only districts on the calendar vote this month.

### 2. Turnout layer (separate from party appeal)

For each block (and chamber):

```text
effective_pop = headcount × turnout_multiplier(block, chamber, global_events)
```

Base ideas:

| Factor | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Guild member | High turnout in guild + district chambers |
| Unaffiliated / non-guild | Low base; boosted by `democratic_awakening` |
| Gang home turf (Pitts) | Gang bonus when **turnout is low**; penalty when turnout is high |
| Corp threat response | If `corp_fear_democrats` high → vote-buying boosts Corp turnout/weight in corp-home districts |

Turnout should be **multiplicative**, easy to tune from events (`Q.turnout_modifiers.dem_awakening += 0.2`).

### 3. Party support (ideology), then fringe vs mainstream

Keep a **party affinity vector** per block (D / I / C / G / H, plus Swing/Apathy if you still want them):

```text
raw_support[p] = base_appeal[p] + regional[p] + demographic[p] + guild[p] + event_delta[p]
```

Then apply a **mainstream curve** per party *within that block*:

- If party is fringe for this block → small slope (±0.1 shift → tiny vote change).
- If mainstream → steep slope (same shift → large swing).

That’s a per-party, per-block logistic (or piecewise linear) with different `steepness[p, block]`, not one shared `find_balance` over seven numbers.

```text
vote_share[p] = softmax( steepness[block][p] × raw_support[p] )
```

Set `steepness` from “historical share” or a tag (`fringe` / `contender` / `dominant`).

### 4. Proportional seats (you already have this piece)

`assign_percentages(vote_totals, n_seats)` is fine for PR. Use it **per chamber** on the vote totals after turnout × support. Don’t reimplement PR until the inputs are stable.

### 5. Staggered district elections

```javascript
Q.election_calendar = {
  Docks: 3, Aurora: 6, Vats: 9, /* month numbers */
}
// each month:
for (district of dueThisMonth(Q.month)) {
  runDistrictElection(district)
}
// executive / guild on their own schedule (annual? biannual?)
```

Only write `Q.Docks_D`, etc. for districts that just voted; others keep previous seats until their month.

### 6. Corporates as three factions (later phase)

Start with one **Corp** bucket + **district corp strength** (Docks vs Vats vs …). When ready, split into Soylent / Magrail / Brazos puppet parties with home-district bonuses. Same pipeline; extra parties in the affinity vector.

---

## How to start (practical order)

Do this entirely in `source/lib/election-model.js` + `npm run simulate-election` until scenarios look right—no Dendry until phase 4+.

**Phase A — Scenarios as tests**  
Write 5–10 named scenarios in comments or a small `scenarios.js`:

1. Baseline 2300: guild-heavy, low mass turnout.  
2. Democratic awakening: mass turnout up, Dems up, rich muted.  
3. Low turnout in Pitts: gangs overperform.  
4. High turnout in Pitts: gangs collapse.  
5. Fringe hate → mainstream hate: small shift vs large seat swing.  
6. One district election month: only Vats seats change.

**Phase B — Minimal new pipeline**  
Replace `find_balance` loop with:

1. Sum effective votes per party per chamber.  
2. `assign_percentages` → seats.  
3. Print report (you already have the CLI).

**Phase C — Turnout only**  
Implement turnout multipliers; verify scenarios 1–4 without changing appeal math much.

**Phase D — Fringe steepness**  
Add per-block party tags; verify scenario 5.

**Phase E — Calendar**  
Partial district updates; verify scenario 6.

**Phase F — Wire to game**  
Swap `root.scene.dry` to call `initElectionModel(Q)` (or sync one thin `{! !}` block). Events only set modifiers (`Q.election.dem_awakening`, `Q.election.corp_vote_buying`), not raw seat counts.

---

## Data you’ll want on each `VoterBlock`

| Field | Role |
|-------|------|
| `demographic`, `area`, `affiliation` | Already have |
| `headcount` | Population × guild share |
| `chamber_weights` | Optional: `{ executive: 2, district: 1 }` for oligarch bias |
| `party_appeal` | Base + deltas (or pointers to shared demographic tables) |
| `party_steepness` | Fringe vs mainstream |
| `turnout_base` | Per chamber |

Global events mutate **tables** (all `first` blocks +0.1 Dem appeal) or **globals** (`mass_turnout += 0.15`), not individual seat qualities—easier to reason about and balance.

---

## What to retire from the current design

- One global logistic balancing seven appeals with a magic `u` loop.  
- Squashing executive, guild, and district into the same tabulation path.  
- Storing final seats only on `Q` without an intermediate “last election snapshot” for debugging.  
- Duplicating logic in `root.scene.dry` and `root_new.scene.dry` (lib-only until the new model is trusted).

---

## Suggested next step

If you want to proceed in-repo, a good first commit is:

1. `source/lib/election-v2.js` — chambers + turnout + PR only, hardcoded 2300 data.  
2. `scripts/simulate-election.js --v2` — run scenarios A1–A3 side by side with v1.

That gives you a clean sandbox for the dynamics you listed without touching Dendry or the card game yet.

I can scaffold `election-v2.js` with the chamber/turnout/PR skeleton and three scenario tests when you’re ready.

<user_query>
with the softmax approach, how would we keep the number of votes from exceeding the number of voters?  Could this system support having some parties (corporate and gang in particular) having vote floors in terms of total votes (but not share of votes) that they can't really fall below?
</user_query>

With softmax, **shares** are automatic; **totals** stay bounded if you treat turnout as the single cap. Vote **floors** are a separate layer you add on top, then re-balance so you still do not exceed the voter pool.

## Keeping votes ≤ voters

Softmax only outputs **proportions** that sum to 1. You never assign “votes” until you multiply by how many people actually voted:

```text
eligible     = headcount × chamber_weight   // who could matter in this chamber
actual_voters = eligible × turnout_rate     // who showed up this election
share[p]      = softmax(score[p])           // Σ share = 1
votes[p]      = actual_voters × share[p]     // Σ votes = actual_voters
```

So by construction, party votes cannot exceed the electorate that turned out, as long as you do not add extra vote mass later without subtracting somewhere else.

Typical pipeline:

```text
scores → softmax → shares (sum to 1)
                  ↓
         × actual_voters
                  ↓
            party vote totals (sum to actual_voters)
                  ↓
         assign_percentages(totals, seats)   // PR on those totals
```

`actual_voters` can differ by block, district, and chamber (guild high turnout, masses low until an awakening, etc.). Softmax does not care; it only splits whatever pool you give it.

---

## Vote floors (minimum total votes, not minimum share)

A **floor** means: “Corp must have at least 8,000 counted votes in this district this cycle,” even if their **share** would be 2%. That is not something softmax does by itself; you add a **floor layer** after or around softmax.

### Pattern A — Reserved ballots, then softmax on the rest (clearest)

```text
actual_voters = 50_000
floor_Corp    = 5_000
floor_Gang    = 2_000
reserved      = floor_Corp + floor_Gang   // 7_000
competitive   = actual_voters - reserved  // 43_000

shares = softmax(scores for Dem, Ind, H, …)   // only parties fighting over competitive pool
votes_Corp = floor_Corp
votes_Gang = floor_Gang
votes_Dem  = competitive × shares.Dem
…
```

- Floors are **absolute** and easy to tune (`Q.election.corp_vote_floor.Pitts = 1200`).
- Softmax still gives PR-like competition for the **remaining** ballots.
- Constraint: `sum(floors) ≤ actual_voters` or you clamp floors / raise turnout.

Corp “vote buying” = raise `floor_Corp` or raise corp turnout in home districts, not a magic appeal knob.

### Pattern B — Softmax first, then bump floors, then trim (flexible, needs one rebalance step)

```text
raw[p]   = actual_voters × softmax(score)[p]
votes[p] = max(floor[p], raw[p])
total    = sum(votes)
if total > actual_voters:
    shrink only parties above their floor until total fits
```

Parties with floors stay at (or above) floor; everyone else absorbs the squeeze. Good when floors are usually small vs total.

### Pattern C — Floors as “base” + competitive softmax (good for lore)

```text
votes[p] = floor[p] + competitive[p]
competitive pool = actual_voters - sum(floor)
competitive = softmax(scores) × competitive pool
```

Corp/gang votes are partly **rigged/base** and partly **normal campaigning**—matches puppet parties and machine politics.

---

## Floors vs shares (why both matter)

| | Share floor | Vote floor |
|---|-------------|------------|
| Meaning | “At least 15% of ballots” | “At least 5,000 ballots” |
| In a tiny election | Same % → fewer votes | Same number → **higher** % |
| In a huge awakening | Same % → many votes | Same number → **lower** % |

Your ask is **vote floors** → use absolute `floor[p]` (optionally per district/chamber), not a minimum softmax weight.

Example: Pitts low turnout, `actual_voters = 10_000`, `floor_Gang = 1_500` → gang is 15% even if scores hate them. Same floor with awakening `actual_voters = 40_000` → gang is 3.75%; share fell, total stayed at 1,500.

That matches “gangs swing **low turnout** elections.”

---

## Making it work with your dynamics

| Dynamic | Where it lives |
|--------|----------------|
| Guild-heavy start | High `turnout` for guild blocks; low for unaffiliated |
| Democratic awakening | Raise mass `turnout`; optional **lower** `chamber_weight` or steepness for rich on Dem appeals |
| Anti-corp / anti-gang backlash | Negative scores in home turf; optionally **lower** corp/gang floors there only |
| Corp escalation | Raise `floor_Corp` or corp turnout when `corp_fear_democrats` is high |
| Xenophobia fringe → threat | Raise Hate **steepness** (mainstream curve), not floor, until movement is entrenched |
| Placated xenophobia helps Dems | Positive Dem score shift, negative Hate shift, no Hate floor |
| Fringe vs mainstream | Per-party `steepness[block][p]` on scores **before** softmax |
| Staggered districts | Only recompute `actual_voters`, floors, scores for districts voting this month |

Executive vs guild vs district: same machinery, different `eligible`, `turnout`, `floor` tables, and seat counts.

---

## Practical recommendation

1. **Always**: `votes = actual_voters × softmax(scores)` so totals are bounded.  
2. **Corp/gang floors**: reserved-ballot model (A) or base + competitive (C).  
3. **Document**: `sum(floors) ≤ actual_voters` per race; cap floors in code if events stack too high.  
4. **Debug in CLI**: print `actual_voters`, each party’s votes, share, and floor contribution—your `simulate-election` path is ideal for this.

If you want to go further next, we can add a tiny `election-v2` sketch in `source/lib/` with `softmax`, `actual_voters`, and `floor_Corp` / `floor_Gang` so you can tune Pitts low-turnout vs awakening in Node before touching Dendry.

<user_query>
I think originally I was wanting to have the interest groups serve as the means of creating this floor.  So voters within the shareholders interest group are going to strongly favor the corporations and give them a floor.  Would this approach be more or less complicated?
</user_query>

**Short answer:** Using interest groups (IGs) as the *source* of corp strength is **simpler conceptually and in your world model**, but **less simple** if you need **guaranteed absolute vote minimums** that never move when turnout explodes. For what you originally wanted, it’s probably the better default; explicit floors are optional seasoning, not the main dish.

## What you’re proposing

Instead of:

```text
votes_Corp = max(floor_Corp, …)
```

you’d have:

```text
votes_Corp = Σ (each voter block in corp-leaning IGs)
             headcount × turnout(IG) × softmax_share(Corp | block)
```

So the “floor” is **emergent**: Gold / Executive (shareholder) blocks with high Corp appeal and high guild turnout always dump a pile of Corp ballots into the total. That matches “interest groups create the floor” much better than a magic `floor_Corp` constant.

## More or less complicated?

| Lens | IG-as-floor | Explicit vote floors |
|------|----------------|----------------------|
| **Lore & mental model** | Less complicated — one story: guilds structure politics | Extra rule: “and also they can’t drop below X” |
| **Data you maintain** | Less complicated — appeals + membership + turnout per IG | More knobs: floors per party × district × event |
| **Guaranteed minimum Corp votes** | More complicated — only approximate unless tuned hard | Less complicated — direct dial |
| **Democratic awakening** | Natural — mass turnout dilutes Corp *share* and can dilute *absolute* Corp votes | You must decide: do floors stay fixed while everyone else grows? |
| **Debugging** | Harder — “why is Corp low?” traces many blocks | Easier — “floor was 5k, competitive pool was …” |
| **Gangs** | Awkward — syndicates aren’t really a guild like Gold/White/Blue | Easier — `floor_Gang` in Pitts |

So: **less complicated overall** for corporations and guild-dominated politics; **more complicated** only where you need hard guarantees or where the force isn’t an IG (gangs in the Pitts).

## How it would work in practice

You already have the right atom: **VoterBlock = demographic × district × interest group**.

Corp strength then comes from **which blocks exist and how they behave**, not a separate floor system:

1. **Membership** — Shareholders / drones / rich skew into Executive + Gold (high `membership` in setup data).
2. **Appeals** — Those IGs have high Corp (and low Dem) in their party score vector.
3. **Turnout** — Guild-linked blocks use high `turnout` for guild and often executive races; unaffiliated uses low turnout until events fire.
4. **Aggregation** — Corp votes = sum of Corp ballots from all blocks; no special case.

That *is* the floor: a **stable bloc** that shows up reliably. You don’t need it to be a fixed 5,000 votes; you need it to be “Corp can’t collapse while the shareholder guild is intact.”

Executive committee can use the same blocks with **extra weight** on rich + Gold (oligarch bias), without a second voting system.

## When IG-as-floor is enough

Good fit if you’re okay with:

- Corp **share** can fall during a big awakening, but **guild machinery** still delivers a solid Corp base.
- Tuning is “Gold membership in this district” + “Corp appeal for Gold” + “guild turnout,” not separate floor tables.
- Events change **appeals and turnout** (`corp_vote_buying` → boost Gold turnout or Corp appeal), not `floor_Corp`.

That’s aligned with “starting vote dominated by special interest groups with high turnout.”

## When you’d still add explicit floors (hybrid)

Consider a small explicit layer only where IGs don’t map cleanly:

- **Gangs** — turf and machine politics, not guild membership. Pitts bonus + low-turnout gang bonus might be **regional/demographic**, with at most a **small** explicit gang base if you want “machine always delivers N ballots.”
- **Corp vote-buying escalation** — optional: IG boost *plus* a temporary `bought_votes` bump when corporations panic about democrats (represents fraud beyond loyal shareholders).
- **Hard narrative guarantee** — “Corp can never go below X in this district” for one plot beat → one-off floor override, not the core model.

## Compared to the magic `u` loop

IG + softmax is **more complicated in lines of code**, but **less complicated in meaning**:

- Each block: scores → softmax → shares → × eligible × turnout → party votes.
- No hidden threshold `u`; behavior comes from **who** the block is (IG, class, district).

The “floor” is **structural** (who’s in Gold and that they vote), not **algorithmic** (search until totals feel right).

## Recommendation

Use **interest groups as the primary floor mechanism** for corporations (and guild seats):

- High guild turnout + corp-leaning appeals on shareholder IGs = corp floor in practice.
- Unaffiliated + low turnout = small democratic mass until awakening raises turnout and steepness for Dems.

Add **explicit vote floors** only for gangs (and maybe emergency corp vote-buying), or skip them and model gangs with **district + turnout** rules (Pitts, low turnout boosts Gang scores or gang “machine” population).

That’s **less complicated** than running two parallel systems (IG world + floor tables) for everything.

If you move to election-v2, a clean split is:

```text
party_votes[p] = Σ_blocks  eligible(block) × turnout(block, chamber) × share(block, p)
```

with **no** `find_balance`; tune floors by tuning **Gold/Executive blocks**, not `max(floor, ·)`.

I can sketch how “shareholder IG” maps to your current Gold/Executive/rich data in a one-page v2 config when you want to start implementing.

Within this system would it make sense to have the VoterBlocks be just Demographic and District and not have an interest group assignment?
</user_query>

Yes — for the model you’re describing, **VoterBlock = demographic × district only** is a good fit. Interest groups stop being a third axis on every person and become **machines that allocate part of each block’s vote** before the competitive pool runs.

## The picture you’re leaning toward

For each block (e.g. first-wave in Docks):

```text
population = 42  (in your 10k units)

1) IG-determined ballots (the “floor”)
   For each interest group G:
     ig_ballots[G] = population × share_in_G × turnout_guild(G) × party_split_G

   Corp’s “floor” is mostly: rich/Gold/Executive shares × high guild turnout × pro-Corp splits
   (summed over all blocks)

2) Competitive pool (the rest)
   competitive_pop = population × (1 − Σ share_in_G)   // or explicit Unaffiliated share

   competitive_ballots[p] = competitive_pop × turnout_competitive × softmax(scores)[p]
```

Total party votes = **sum of IG-determined Corp (etc.)** + **competitive Corp**, then PR for seats in that chamber.

That matches “guilds fix part of the outcome; everyone else fights over what’s left, often with low turnout.”

## Why drop IG from VoterBlock?

| IG on every block (today) | Demo × district only |
|---------------------------|----------------------|
| Same person counted in Gold, White, Blue paths as separate blocks | One headcount per cell |
| “Floor” is a side effect of summing many blocks | Floor is an explicit **phase** |
| 7×7×5 ≈ 245 units | 7×7 = **49** units |
| IG feels like a place people live | IG feels like an **institution** that claims loyalty |

Conceptually, IGs are **how much of this cell’s vote is already spoken for**, not a place in space. Keeping them off the block type makes that obvious in code and when balancing.

## What each thing holds

**VoterBlock** `(demographic, district)`:

- `population`
- Competitive party **scores** (demographic + district + events)
- Optional **per-cell** IG membership shares; if you don’t need that yet, **per-demographic** shares applied in every district (what your setup data already looks like)

**InterestGroup** (separate objects, not block tags):

- `party_split` — how this IG’s determined ballots break (Corp-heavy for Gold, etc.)
- `turnout` — high for guild machinery
- `membership[stratum]` — share of each demographic in this IG (your current membership arrays)

**Competitive electorate** (per block or global):

- `turnout_competitive` — low at start; awakening raises it
- `steepness[party]` — fringe vs mainstream for the competitive pool only

## Does it still give corp/gang “floors”?

**Corporations:** Yes, without a `floor_Corp` constant. Shareholder-skewed demographics × Gold/Executive membership × guild turnout × pro-Corp IG split adds up to a **stable Corp ballot base** every cycle.

**Gangs:** Still awkward as a pure IG (syndicate ≠ guild). Reasonable split:

- **IG path:** none or a loose “machine” IG if you invent one  
- **Competitive path:** Pitts (and similar) modifiers + **low-turnout bonus** on Gang scores in the competitive pool  

So gang “floor” is mostly **regional + turnout rules** on demo×district blocks, not Gold-style IG reservation.

## One design choice to decide early

Are IG-determined ballots **the same in every chamber**?

Often you want:

| Chamber | IG-determined share | Competitive share |
|---------|---------------------|-------------------|
| **Guild seats** | ~100% (only guild-eligible pool) | ~0% |
| **Executive** | Large (wealth + shareholder IGs, weighted) | Smaller |
| **District** | Smaller IG slice (floor) | Most of the race |

Same 49 blocks; **chamber** picks different `turnout_guild`, weights, and how much of the cell is “spoken for” vs competitive. You don’t need IG on the block for that—only chamber config.

## Caveat: membership must sum sensibly

Per demographic (or per block):

```text
share_Executive + share_Gold + share_White + share_Blue + share_competitive ≈ 1
```

`Unaffiliated` can be explicit or “whatever’s left.” Competitive vote only runs on that remainder—otherwise you double-count people.

## Verdict

**Yes, it makes sense** to make VoterBlocks **demographic × district only** and treat interest groups as **floor allocators** on top of each block, with a **second-pass competitive softmax** on the non-IG population.

That’s **simpler** than triple-axis blocks and **clearer** than bolt-on vote floors, as long as you’re fine with corp strength being **structural** (tune via IG membership and turnout) rather than a fixed “minimum 5,000 votes” unless you add a small gang/machine exception.

A natural v2 pipeline:

```text
for each VoterBlock:
  ig_votes     = allocate_via_interest_groups(block, chamber)
  comp_votes   = competitive_softmax(block, chamber)
  total_votes  = ig_votes + comp_votes   // capped at population × turnout_cap

aggregate → assign_percentages → Q.Exec_*, Q.Gold_*, Q.Docks_*, …
```

If you want to implement next, we can scaffold that in `election-v2.js` with 49 blocks and three chamber configs, still runnable via `npm run simulate-election`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
One-time backfill: import Cursor agent-transcript JSONL into .cursor/conversation-history/

Usage (from repo root):
  python3 .cursor/hooks/backfill-transcript.py
  python3 .cursor/hooks/backfill-transcript.py /path/to/session.jsonl
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
HISTORY = ROOT / ".cursor" / "conversation-history"
SESSIONS = HISTORY / "sessions"
TRANSCRIPTS = (
    Path.home() / ".cursor" / "projects" / "home-airy-mikasa" / "agent-transcripts"
)


def utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def find_latest_transcript() -> Path | None:
    if not TRANSCRIPTS.exists():
        return None
    candidates = list(TRANSCRIPTS.glob("*/*.jsonl"))
    if not candidates:
        return None
    return max(candidates, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)


def content_to_text(content) -> str:
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if not isinstance(content, list):
        return json.dumps(content, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    parts = []
    for item in content:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            parts.append(str(item))
            continue
        kind = item.get("type", "text")
        if kind == "text":
            parts.append(item.get("text", ""))
        elif kind == "tool_use":
            name = item.get("name", "tool")
            inp = item.get("input", {})
            parts.append(
                f"**Tool:** `{name}`\n\n```json\n"
                + json.dumps(inp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                + "\n```"
            )
        elif kind == "tool_result":
            parts.append(
                "**Tool result:**\n\n```\n"
                + str(item.get("text", item.get("content", "")))[:12000]
                + "\n```"
            )
        else:
            parts.append(f"_{kind}_\n```json\n{json.dumps(item, indent=2)}\n```")
    return "\n\n".join(p for p in parts if p)


def backfill(jsonl_path: Path, session_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    session_id = session_id or jsonl_path.parent.name
    md_path = SESSIONS / f"{session_id}.md"
    out_jsonl = SESSIONS / f"{session_id}.jsonl"
    SESSIONS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    lines_in = jsonl_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    md_parts = [
        f"# Conversation session `{session_id}` (backfilled)",
        f"\n_Source: `{jsonl_path}`_",
        f"\n_Imported {utc_now()}_",
        "\n\n> Note: Cursor transcript exports may redact thinking blocks. "
        "Live `afterAgentThought` hooks capture full chain-of-thought going forward.\n",
    ]

    with out_jsonl.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as jf:
        for i, line in enumerate(lines_in):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            row = json.loads(line)
            role = row.get("role", "unknown")
            msg = row.get("message", {})
            text = content_to_text(msg.get("content", msg))
            ts = utc_now()
            entry = {
                "timestamp": ts,
                "event": "transcript_import",
                "role": role,
                "text": text,
                "line": i + 1,
            }
            jf.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            md_parts.append(f"\n## [{ts}] {role} (imported line {i + 1})\n\n{text}\n")

    md_path.write_text("".join(md_parts), encoding="utf-8")
    pointer = HISTORY / "current-session.json"
    pointer.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "session_id": session_id,
                "md_log": str(md_path.relative_to(ROOT)),
                "jsonl_log": str(out_jsonl.relative_to(ROOT)),
                "backfilled_from": str(jsonl_path),
                "backfilled_at": utc_now(),
            },
            indent=2,
        )
        + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return md_path, out_jsonl


def main() -> int:
    src = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else find_latest_transcript()
    if not src or not src.exists():
        print("No transcript found.", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Looked in: {TRANSCRIPTS}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    md, jl = backfill(src)
    print(f"Backfilled {src}")
    print(f"  -> {md}")
    print(f"  -> {jl}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

is **not** standard JavaScript. Nothing in the JS language defines `Q`.

It comes from **Dendrynexus / Dendry**: the engine exposes a **game state object** named `Q`, and your `.dry` scenes read and write it. The project cheat sheet describes it as the main namespace for stats (`Q.month`, `Q.update_projections()`, etc.). The “Q” name fits **qualities** — numeric stats that pair with `source/qdisplays/*.qdisplay.dry` for labels like `[+ month : month +]`.

**How it works in practice**

1. **Engine layer** — Dendrynexus gives you a global `Q` (like a built-in `game` or `state` in other engines).
2. **Your game layer** — `root.scene.dry` / `root_new.scene.dry` hang a lot on it: election code, `Q.first`, `Q.stratums`, functions like `Q.update_projections`, and so on. That part is **this project’s** design, not something every Dendry game must copy.
3. **Scene layer** — Events/cards do `on-arrival: Q.soylent_anger += 0.1` or `{! Q.first["Dems"] += 2 !}` — normal property access on that object.

**Python analogy**

Think of `Q` as a big module-level namespace or a `types.SimpleNamespace()` the engine owns:

```python
# conceptual — not real Dendry API
Q.month = 3
Q.soylent_anger += 0.1
Q.update_projections()
```

**Not the same as**

- `import Q` from a library
- A JS keyword
- Required naming (another Dendry game could still use `Q` because the engine does)

**Style note from your repo**

In `{! … !}` blocks you can use full JS (`function`, `class`, `const`). In short `on-arrival:` lines you often assign without `let`/`const` — Dendrynexus runs those updates against the global/`Q` scope so `soylent_anger += 0.1` means “bump the quality on game state,” not “create a new local variable.”

So: **`Q` = Dendrynexus game state; what’s *on* `Q` = mostly Autumn’s Mikasa model plus whatever you add.**

`root_new` already does a **layered sum** when it polls: each `VoterBlock` combines demographic + district + block + global `competitiveScores`, then softmax. The design question is really: **where do event choices store their deltas, and when do those become that sum?**

---

## Your two approaches, named clearly

| Approach | What happens on a choice | When math runs |
|----------|---------------------------|----------------|
| **A. Direct / bundler** | Event calls something like `shiftBlockAppeal(block, 'D', +0.3)` or `Q.alien.Dems += 2` | Immediately or on next `update_projections` |
| **B. Modifier ledger** | Event adds `{ scope: 'stratum', target: 'alien', party: 'D', delta: 2, source: 'orc_marriage2' }` | On `update_projections`, recompute all layers from base + active modifiers |

You’re not wrong that B fits “define the rules in root, events only add deltas.” That’s the usual pattern in sims and games.

---

## Best-practice lens (not religion)

**1. Single source of truth**  
Right now you can touch the same voter mood via `Q.first["Dems"]`, `demographic.competitiveScores`, and (in theory) `block.competitiveScores`. Pick **one pipeline** and treat the others as derived or legacy.

**2. Content vs engine**  
`.dry` scenes should say *what* changed (“alien stratum likes Dems more”), not *how* 49 blocks get updated. A small API on `Q` keeps scales and party keys consistent (fixes orc_marriage2’s `+=0.2` vs `+=5` problem).

**3. Recompute vs accumulate**  
- **Accumulate forever:** every choice does `+=` on live scores → simple, but hard to debug, undo, or rebalance.  
- **Recompute from base + modifiers:** each poll: `effective = base + sum(modifiers)` → slightly more code, much easier to inspect and tune.

**4. Match granularity to design**  
Most of your events are **stratum** (“first wave”, “alien”), **district** (“Vats”, “Pitts”), or **global** (xenophobia, economy). Very few need a single `Docks_coop` block. Default API should be stratum/district/global, not per-block, unless you have a rare hyper-local effect.

**5. Centralize rules, distribute data**  
Put in `root_new` (or `election-v2.js`):

- how layers combine (you already have this),
- how modifiers stack (add? cap? multiply?),
- helper functions.

Put in events/cards:

- only **instances** (“+2 Dems appeal for alien”).

Defining *every* event’s numbers in root is usually wrong—that becomes a giant switch. Defining *how modifiers work* in root is right.

---

## Recommendation for Mikasa: **B, layered, with a thin bundler**

Use a **modifier ledger** aligned with layers you already have:

```text
base (init config, _baseCompetitiveScores)
  + demographic modifiers  (stratum: first, alien, …)
  + district modifiers     (Docks, Pitts, …)
  + global modifiers       (Q.global_shifts / scenario)
  → demographic.competitiveScores / district / global
  → blockCompetitiveScores(block)  // sum layers, then softmax per block
```

Events don’t touch `VoterBlock` directly. They call one bundler:

```javascript
// conceptual API on Q after init
Q.shiftElectorate({
  stratum: 'alien',   // or district: 'Aurora', or global: true
  party: 'D',         // or label: 'Dems' if you keep legacy names
  competitive: 1.0,   // logits-scale delta (document one scale!)
  id: 'orc_marriage2_modern',  // optional, for removal/stacking
})
```

`update_projections` / `runElectionsAndWriteQ` already runs before tabulation—add **`rebuildCompetitiveLayers(state)`** there that:

1. Resets each demographic/district/global to `_base*`.
2. Applies all entries in `electionState.modifiers` (or `Q.electorateModifiers`).
3. Optionally syncs legacy `Q.alien.Dems` from modifiers for old scenes, or migrates scenes to the API.

That’s approach **B** with the ergonomics of approach **A** (one function call per choice).

---

## When direct `VoterBlock` writes make sense

Use block-level only for:

- “this district×stratum cell only” (rare),
- temporary combat-campaign buffs,
- debugging.

Otherwise you maintain 49×5 numbers mentally for no gain—blocks already inherit stratum + district.

---

## Other patterns worth knowing

| Pattern | Fit for you |
|--------|-------------|
| **Intent queue** | Choice pushes `{ op: 'shift', … }`; month tick applies queue. Good if effects should lag until “polling day.” |
| **Tagged modifiers with expiry** | `{ untilMonth: 2302, … }` for refugee crisis, convention fallout. Fits phase 3 in `plan.txt`. |
| **Derived stats bridge** | `second_wave_dissent` doesn’t touch election; monthly tick adds modifiers from thresholds (`if dissent > 50 → global Hate +0.5`). Unifies community placeholders with B. |
| **Immutable event effects table in root** | `EFFECTS.orc_marriage2_modern = [{ stratum:'alien', party:'D', … }]`; scene calls `applyEffect('orc_marriage2_modern')`. Data central, content thin—nice for balance passes. |
| **Keep legacy labels only** | Continue `Q.first["Dems"]` + `syncVoteAppealsToCompetitive`—minimal change, but modifiers and v2 scores stay two parallel systems (what you have now). |

---

## Practical first step (small, not a rewrite)

1. **Pick one scale** — e.g. competitive logits (−2…+2), not mixed 0.2 and 5 on `Dems`.  
2. **Add `Q.shiftElectorate(...)`** in `root_new` that appends to `electionState.modifiers`.  
3. **Add `rebuildCompetitiveLayers()`** at the start of `runElectionsAndWriteQ` (before `engine.runAll`).  
4. **Migrate one event** (`orc_marriage2`) to the API; leave `syncAllVoteAppeals` as bridge until old `Q.first["Dems"]` writes are gone.  
5. **Document modifier kinds** in a comment block in root: `stratum | district | global | ig_turnout | …`.

---

## Direct answer to “which approach?”

- **Not** “events write each VoteBlock” as the default—that fights your strata×district model and duplicates layers.  
- **Yes** “list of modifiers, tally on poll”—that *is* good practice here, especially since `blockCompetitiveScores` is already a tally of layers.  
- **Best UX for you:** modifier ledger + **`Q.shiftElectorate` bundler** so `.dry` stays one-liners and root owns the math.

If you want to implement next, we can sketch the exact `modifiers[]` shape and `rebuildCompetitiveLayers` against your current `Demographic` / `District` classes without touching every scene at once.

Yes — there are solid third paths. And **post_event is a good place for some of the pipeline, but not for defining every event’s deltas.**

---

## Third options (beyond direct blocks vs modifier list)

### 3. **Derived / rule-based (no explicit modifier list)**

Events only change **story stats** (`second_wave_dissent`, `patriot_meme_strength`, `soylent_anger`). On poll, **formulas** turn those into appeals:

```text
if Q.second_wave_dissent > 40 → global Hate += 0.3
if Q.soylent_anger > 0.2 → drone stratum Corp += 0.5
```

No per-choice modifier rows; one table in root defines the mapping.  
**Pros:** Fewer one-off API calls; community/meme vars become meaningful.  
**Cons:** Harder to do one-off story beats (“this bill only helps aliens +5”); tuning is indirect.

---

### 4. **Flags + effect table (data in root, triggers in scenes)**

Choices set flags: `Q.orc_marriage2_choice = 'modern'`.  
Root (or a JS module) holds:

```javascript
EFFECTS.orc_marriage2_modern = [
  { stratum: 'alien', party: 'D', delta: 1.0 },
  ...
]
```

`applyPendingEffects()` runs on poll and applies rows for set flags.  
**Pros:** Balance in one file; scenes stay tiny.  
**Cons:** Every branch needs a flag name; easy to forget to clear one-shot flags.

---

### 5. **Hook pipeline (ordered phases)**

`update_projections` becomes:

1. `applyEventModifiers()` — ledger from choices  
2. `applyDerivedRules()` — dissent → hate  
3. `applyEconomyTick()` — protest_good, etc.  
4. `rebuildLayers()` → `engine.runAll()`

**Pros:** Clear extension points; mix ledger + derived.  
**Cons:** Order matters; document the pipeline once.

---

### 6. **Intent queue (deferred until month end)**

Choices push to `Q.electorateQueue.push({...})`; nothing hits appeals until poll.  
**Pros:** Matches “polling updated at month end”; can batch/cancel.  
**Cons:** Player doesn’t see seat change until post_event (may be what you want).

---

**Practical combo for Mikasa:** **5 (pipeline) + 4 (effect table for big events) + 3 (derived rules for wave/meme/corp anger)**. Modifier ledger is still the right core for one-off story shifts; derived rules absorb the redundant placeholders.

---

## Should all modifiers live in `post_event.scene.dry`?

**Flow today:** advance month → `post_event` → `Q.update_projections()` → maybe more `#event` scenes → main.

```5:7:source/scenes/post_event.scene.dry
Q.update_projections();
```

That comment matches “update numbers after events” — but **choices already ran** in the card/event scene. `post_event` wasn’t in the loop for those choices unless you only advance month once per “turn.”

| Put in **post_event** | Put in **choice `on-arrival`** (or bundler) | Put in **root / election-v2.js** |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Call `rebuildCompetitiveLayers()` + `update_projections()` | Record *what happened*: flag, queue entry, `Q.shiftElectorate(...)` | *How* modifiers stack, bases, softmax, IG math |
| Month tick: expire modifiers, `organize_tick`, derived rules | Narrative-specific deltas tied to that button | `EFFECTS` table, dissent→appeal formulas |
| Bridge: `meme_strength` → modifiers before poll | | `Q.shiftElectorate` implementation |

**Defining all modifiers in post_event** only works if you mean:

1. **All reconciliation logic** — yes, good home: one place that runs before `update_projections()`.  
2. **All numeric definitions for every event choice** — no: post_event doesn’t know you picked `@permit` unless the convention scene set `Q.september_convention = 'permit'`. You’d end up with a huge `if` ladder that duplicates event knowledge.

Better split:

```text
Event choice  →  Q.shiftElectorate(...) or Q.flags / queue
post_event    →  reconcileDerived(), expireModifiers(), then update_projections()
root_new      →  math + modifier types + optional EFFECTS table
```

So post_event becomes **“poll tick”**, not **“author every event here.”**

---

## When post_event-only *does* make sense

- Effects are **monthly**, not per choice (inflation, refugee pressure tick, corp war phase).  
- Everything is **computed from Q** with no per-choice memory.  
- You want **one** `update_projections()` and derived rules so individual scenes never forget to call it (you already call it in post_event; Dundalk is the outlier that calls it mid-event).

---

## Short recommendation

1. **Third option to add:** derived rules (meme/dissent/anger → appeals) + optional effect table keyed by flags.  
2. **post_event:** run the full pipeline once per month end; don’t move event-authored deltas there unless they’re flag-driven formulas.  
3. **Choices:** thin writes (`Q.shiftElectorate` or set flag + `applyEffect(id)`).  
4. **root_new:** owns stacking, rebuild, and `update_projections` implementation.

If you implement one thing first: extend `runElectionsAndWriteQ` with `rebuildFromModifiers()` and call that from `post_event` right before `update_projections()` (and eventually remove duplicate calls from individual events).

Yes. In JavaScript you can use **positional constructor arguments** so each modifier is one line and the catalog reads like a table.

**Order:**

```text
new ElectorateModifier(id, scope, target, party, delta [, activeIf])
```

- **`scope`:** `'stratum'`, `'district'`, or `'global'`
- **`target`:** stratum or district id; use `''` for global
- **`party`:** `'D'`, `'I'`, `'C'`, `'G'`, `'H'`
- **`activeIf`:** optional 6th argument; omit it if the modifier is always on

The class still accepts the old `{ id, scope, … }` object if you pass a single object as the first argument.

Yes for the *idea*, but **not with the code as written today**.

### What happens now

`alien_dems_feb2300 += 1` in a `.dry` `on-arrival` only bumps a property on `Q` (if Dendry allows it — usually it does, same as `budget += 2`).

The catalog row named `alien_dems_feb2300` **does not read that property**. It uses:

- fixed `delta: 0.2`
- `activeIf` (date check)

So `+= 1` on `Q` right now **does not change the election** unless you wire it.

### Pattern you’re describing (good fit)

Treat each catalog `id` as a **strength counter** on `Q`:

```dry
on-arrival: alien_dems_feb2300 += 1
```

On poll, `applyElectorateModifiers` does something like:

```text
effectiveShift = catalog.delta * (Q[modifier.id] || 0)
```

No need to “detect updates” — Dendry doesn’t push diffs into JS. Every `Q.update_projections()` **re-reads current `Q`** and rebuilds from base + modifiers. That *is* the sync.

Flow:

```text
Event choice  →  Q.alien_dems_feb2300 += 1
post_event    →  update_projections()
                 → applyElectorateModifiers() reads Q.* and applies
```

### `+= 1` vs flags

| Style | Dendry | Catalog |
|--------|--------|---------|
| **Counter** | `alien_dems_feb2300 += 1` | row defines scope/target/party/**per-stack delta** |
| **Flag** | `Q.september_convention = 'permit'` | `activeIf(q) { return q.september_convention === 'permit' }` |

Counters stack when the same thing can fire multiple times; flags fit one-off branches.

You can combine them: only apply if `Q[id] > 0` **and** optional `activeIf`.

### Applying a modifier “multiple times”

Depends what “multiple” means:

1. **Same month, several `+= 1`** (e.g. two events)  
   - `Q.alien_dems_feb2300` becomes `2` → apply `2 × 0.2` if you use counter × delta.  
   - Intended if you want effects to stack.

2. **Same counter, every poll, no new `+=`**  
   - Rebuild runs each month; counter stays `2` → **same boost every month** until you clear or decay it.  
   - Not “applied twice in one poll” — applied once per poll with strength `2`.

3. **Catalog row + `activeIf` always true, no counter**  
   - Every poll adds `0.2` again from that row (same each time, not cumulative unless `Q[id]` grows).

4. **Same event visited twice** (`max-visits` wrong)  
   - `+= 1` twice → counter stacks; can be a bug or intentional.

**Complications to plan for:**

- **Initialize** `Q.alien_dems_feb2300 = 0` (root or first post_event) so `+=` isn’t `undefined + 1`.
- **Id must match** catalog `id` exactly.
- **Drift** — uncapped `+=` over years can explode; consider caps, one-shot flags, or monthly decay in post_event.
- **Mixing models** — row with `activeIf` date *and* `Q[id]` counter can double-count if both apply; pick one driver per row.
- **Magnitude** — is `+= 1` “one stack of 0.2 logits” or “+1.0 logit”? Define per row (`delta` × stacks vs `Q[id]` is the whole shift).

### Recommendation

- **One-off choices:** set a flag; catalog uses `activeIf` (your commented `september_permit` line).
- **Stackable influence:** `modifier_id += 1` and teach `apply()` to use `delta * (Q[this.id] || 0)` when `Q[this.id] > 0`.

That’s a small change to `ElectorateModifier.apply` and init lines for each catalog id — say if you want it wired in.

can you suggest a way to revise the ElectorateModifier so that a bunch of modifiers could be setup to be invoked by the same ID?  So for instance there could be an ID favor_second_wave_housing_dispute which would increase second wave support for Dems in Aurora but decrease first wave support for Dems in Aurora.  If I understand the code correctly, this would require two modifiers and thus two ids.  Could one modifier be made a child of another or a modifier be given multiple effects?  What is the best approach here?

Here’s how the pieces fit, then a concrete recommendation.

## What one row does today

One `ElectorateModifier` = one **`id`** = one **`Q[id]`** stack counter = one **(scope, target, party, delta)**.

So `favor_second_wave_housing_dispute` with two opposing shifts needs **two rows** only if each row has its **own** `id`. With the current code, two rows with **different** ids means two counters (`foo += 1` and `bar += 1`), not one story choice.

“Aurora + second wave vs first wave” is also **two dimensions**:

- **Stratum** (`second`, `first`) → `demographic.competitiveScores`
- **District** (`Aurora`) → `district.competitiveScores`

Every **block** in Aurora gets that district layer; every **block** with stratum `second` gets that stratum layer everywhere. There is no “only Aurora×second” in the catalog unless you add block-level effects later. For “housing dispute in Aurora,” you often want something like:

- `district` `Aurora` `D` +X  
- `stratum` `second` `D` +Y  
- `stratum` `first` `D` −Z  

—all driven by the **same** story bump.

---

## Options

| Approach | Idea | Pros | Cons |
|----------|------|------|------|
| **A. Shared `stackId`** | Several rows; stacks read from `Q[stackId]`, row `id` is just a label | Table stays one line per effect; one `+= 1` in Dendry | More rows in the catalog |
| **B. Multi-effect row** | One id, `effects: [[scope,target,party,delta], …]` | One catalog entry per story choice | Harder to keep as a neat column table |
| **C. Parent / child** | Bundle row + child rows | Nice for grouping in source | Same as B after flatten; extra concept |
| **D. Two ids** | `favor_…_second += 1` and `favor_…_first += 1` | No code change | Easy to forget one bump; not one choice |

**Child-of-parent** is mostly authoring sugar: at poll time you still want “read `Q[favor_second_wave_housing_dispute]`, apply N deltas.” That’s **A or B** under the hood.

---

## Best fit for your setup: **shared `stackId` (A)**

Keep **one effect per line** (readable table), add a **`stackId`** (name it what you like) that is the **Q quality** events bump:

```text
// label (optional) | stackId (= Q) | scope | target | party | delta
new ElectorateModifier('aurora_second_dems_up', 'favor_second_wave_housing_dispute', 'stratum', 'second', 'D', 0.2),
new ElectorateModifier('aurora_first_dems_down', 'favor_second_wave_housing_dispute', 'stratum', 'first', 'D', -0.15),
new ElectorateModifier('aurora_dems_up', 'favor_second_wave_housing_dispute', 'district', 'Aurora', 'D', 0.1),
```

Dendry:

```dry
on-arrival: favor_second_wave_housing_dispute += 1
```

Poll: each row uses `stacksFromQ(q, 'favor_second_wave_housing_dispute')` → same stack count → `shift = delta * stacks` per row.

Positional shape could be:

```text
new ElectorateModifier(rowId, stackId, scope, target, party, delta [, activeIf])
```

- **`rowId`**: optional debug name (can equal `stackId` for simple cases).  
- **`stackId`**: must match the Q property you `+=`.

That’s better than parent/child for you: no tree to walk, still grep-friendly.

---

## When to use **multi-effect (B)** instead

Use **one modifier, many effects** when the bundle is **always** defined together and you don’t want three lines to get out of sync:

```javascript
new ElectorateModifier('favor_second_wave_housing_dispute', [
    ['stratum', 'second', 'D', 0.2],
    ['stratum', 'first', 'D', -0.15],
    ['district', 'Aurora', 'D', 0.1],
])
```

One `+= 1`, one place to read the whole choice. Tradeoff: less “spreadsheet” and a tiny bit more structure in the constructor.

A small helper keeps it one logical line:

```javascript
function EM(stackId, spec) { return spec.map(function (row) {
    return new ElectorateModifier(stackId + '_' + row[1] + '_' + row[2], stackId, row[0], row[1], row[2], row[3])
})}
```

…then flatten into `Q.electorateModifierCatalog`.

---

## Recommendation

- **Default: A (`stackId`)** — multiple rows, one Q counter, matches Dendry `+= 1` and your table style.  
- **Optional: B** for large fixed bundles you want atomic in one definition.  
- **Skip parent/child** unless you want UI/grouping in the file; runtime can flatten bundles the same as A.

If you want this in code next, the minimal change is: add `stackId` (default `stackId === id` so old rows keep working), `stacksFromQ(q, this.stackId)`, and the three-line `favor_second_wave_housing_dispute` example in the catalog.

**Python decorators aren’t built into JavaScript**, but the same idea — “run the normal step, then wrap or replace behavior for special cases” — is common. For drone voting, that’s a reasonable way to think about it.

### JS equivalents to decorators

| Python-ish idea | JavaScript |
|-----------------|------------|
| `@wrap` on one function | Higher-order function: `const tabulate = withDroneRule(tabulateBlock)` |
| Method decoration | Wrap a method on the engine, or call a hook list after `allocateCompetitiveVotes` |
| Class decorator | No native support; you’d patch the prototype or use a subclass |
| Per-type rule | **Config + hook** on `Demographic` (often clearest for games) |

So yes: a **wrapper function** or a **post-step hook** is the JS version of a decorator.

### What fits `root_new` best

Your pipeline is already a chain:

```text
tabulateBlock → IG votes + competitive softmax → (optional transforms) → chamber totals
```

A decorator-style rule would sit **after** competitive votes are computed for a block (or after the full block total), and only when `block.demographic.id === 'drone'`:

```javascript
function withDemographicVoteRules(tabulateFn) {
    return function (block, ...rest) {
        var result = tabulateFn(block, ...rest)
        if (block.demographic.id === 'drone') {
            result = applyDroneVoteContract(result, block, ...)
        }
        return result
    }
}
```

Or a **hook list** (very game-engine friendly):

```javascript
// root_new
const BLOCK_VOTE_RULES = [
    applyDroneCorpOrAbstainRule,
    // applySyndicateBriberyRule later
]

function tabulateBlock(...) {
    var result = { ig, comp, total }
    for (var rule of BLOCK_VOTE_RULES) {
        result = rule(block, result, state, chamber) || result
    }
    return result
}
```

That’s not literally `@decorator`, but it’s the same composition: one place registers rules, tabulation stays dumb.

### Decorator vs config on `Demographic`

For “drones only Corp or abstain,” you could also put on the stratum config:

```javascript
drone: {
    igClaimCap: 0.8,
    competitiveVoteRule: 'corp_or_abstain',
}
```

Then one function dispatches on `competitiveVoteRule`. That’s less “decorator,” more **strategy pattern** — often easier to read in a `.dry` / data-driven game than a pile of wrappers.

### Abstain in v2

Old code used **Apathy** as abstain. v2 competitive math only has **D/I/C/G/H**. A drone rule needs a defined behavior, e.g.:

- non‑Corp competitive share → **not counted** (turnout waste / abstain), or  
- force softmax to **C only** on the competitive slice, or  
- split IG vs competitive differently.

The decorator/hook should implement that policy in **one function**, not spread across events.

### Recommendation

- **Yes**, use a **single hook or wrapper** for demographic-specific vote law — decorator-shaped, implemented as `BLOCK_VOTE_RULES` or `withVoteRules(tabulateBlock)`.
- **Don’t** rely on JS decorator syntax (stage-3 decorators exist but aren’t worth it here).
- Keep **baseline leans** in `buildDemographics`; use the hook for **hard rules** (corp-or-abstain), and **modifiers** for story shifts (`drone_syndicate_bribery += 1` lowering effective Corp turnout, etc.).

If you want this wired next, the small version is one `applyDroneCorpOrAbstainRule(block, compVotes, igVotes)` called from `tabulateBlock` before summing `total`.

### How it works
After each block’s IG + competitive votes are computed, `applyBlockVoteRules` runs every function in `BLOCK_VOTE_RULES` in order.

**`applyDroneCorpOrAbstainRule`** (when `demographic.voteRule === 'corp_or_abstain'`):
- Zeros **D, I, G, H** on both `ig` and `comp` (abstain — those ballots don’t count)
- Keeps **C** only
- Rebuilds `total` from the filtered `ig` + `comp`

Drone stratum in `buildDemographics`:

```javascript
voteRule: 'corp_or_abstain',
```

Other strata can get new rules by setting `voteRule` or adding functions to `BLOCK_VOTE_RULES`.

### Adding another rule later
```javascript
function applySyndicateDroneBriberyRule(block, result, state, chamber) {
    // ...
    return result
}

const BLOCK_VOTE_RULES = [
    applyDroneCorpOrAbstainRule,
    applySyndicateDroneBriberyRule,
]
```

Each rule: `(block, result, state, chamber) → result`, with `{ ig, comp, total }` party vote objects.

v2 CLI sim still runs cleanly with this in place. Syndicate bribery lowering drone Corp turnout would be a separate rule or a modifier on `Q` + competitive turnout — not added yet.

### How v2 splits each block

For each `VoterBlock` (stratum × district):

1. **IG floor** — Up to `igClaimCap` of the population is claimed by interest groups. Those ballots use `ig.turnout` (often ~0.88–0.98) and fixed `partyShares`.

2. **Competitive pool** — The rest: `(1 - claimedFraction) × population`.

3. **Competitive turnout** — Only part of that pool actually votes:

```605:633:source/scenes/root_new.scene.dry
function allocateCompetitiveVotes(block, interestGroups, chamber, state) {
    ...
    const competitivePop = block.population * (1 - claimed) * VOTE_SCALE
    ...
    let turnout = competitiveTurnout(block, chamber, state)
    ...
    const ballots = competitivePop * turnout
    for (const k of PARTY_KEYS) {
        votes[k] += ballots * shares[k]
    }
```

So `(1 - turnout)` of the **competitive pool** never gets ballots — they don’t go to any party. That’s implicit abstention on the competitive slice, not a labeled “Apathy” vote.

Chamber defaults already keep competitive participation low in places:

| Chamber    | `competitiveTurnout` |
|-----------|----------------------|
| Executive | 0.35                 |
| Guild     | 0.05                 |
| District  | 0.40                 |

With high `igClaimCap` (e.g. drone 0.8), most people never reach the competitive pool at all; of the remainder, only 35% (executive) might vote. That’s why IGs dominate early — by design, not a bug.

### What isn’t modeled

- **No Apathy / Swing party** in v2 (only D/I/C/G/H). Non-voters aren’t a sixth tally.
- **No third “disengaged” slice** — everyone is assumed either IG-claimed or in the competitive pool; the model doesn’t track “doesn’t participate in either channel.”
- **No automatic phase-1 penalty** — `state.global.competitiveTurnout` defaults to `1` in `electionState`; organizing phase doesn’t further suppress competitive vote unless you lower that from events/modifiers/`Q.phase`.
- **Drone `corp_or_abstain`** — strips non-Corp competitive/IG votes; that’s “invalid ballot,” not the same as low turnout.

### Early game (organizing / phase 1)

You already get IG-heavy results from **high claim + low chamber competitiveTurnout**. To make phase 1 even more IG-dominated, lower competitive participation globally, e.g. in `runElectionsAndWriteQ` or via a modifier:

```javascript
// example: while organizing
electionState.global.competitiveTurnout = (Q.phase === 1) ? 0.5 : 1
```

Or a catalog row / `Q.organizing_low_turnout` stack that bumps `competitiveTurnoutBonus` negative on `state.global`.

### Summary

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Do competitive votes respect non-voters? | **Yes**, via `competitiveTurnout` — unused competitive-pool population never enters softmax. |
| Is that visible as Apathy? | **No** — those ballots simply aren’t cast. |
| Does that support early IG dominance? | **Yes**, together with `igClaimCap` and low chamber rates. |
| Wired to `Q.phase === 1` yet? | **Not automatically** — easy add on `state.global`. |

If you want this tightened up in code, sensible next steps are: (1) phase-based `state.global.competitiveTurnout` when `Q.phase === 1`, and/or (2) optional `compAbstainBallots` on `tabulateBlock` results for debugging/UI. Say which you prefer and we can add it.

[REDACTED]

Sounds good. When you tune early game, `competitiveTurnout` on each chamber and `igClaimCap` per stratum are the main levers; phase or modifiers on `state.global.competitiveTurnout` are there if you want organizing to feel even more IG-heavy later.

| `cards/organizing/coop_economy.scene.dry`, `magic.scene.dry` | Choices without `@` subscenes | Added minimal stub subscenes |
| `cards/organizing/education.scene.dry` | `chose-if` / `on-arrival: TBD`; prose glued to properties; missing `@too_broke` | Valid `choose-if` / `on-arrival`; blank lines before body; `@too_broke` stub at end |

### Notes on “error comments”

`#` lines **inside** `@subscene` property blocks break Dendry (they get parsed as properties). `#` at the **root** (choice list / between scenes) is fine — see `activist_training.scene.dry`. I dropped most inline `# dendry: …` notes for that reason. **`available-if` is not supported** by the installed dendrynexus; use **`choose-if` + `unavailable-subtitle`** instead (worth updating `.cursor/rules/dendry.mdc` if you want the cheat sheet accurate).

The warning came from **Winston 0.8**, pulled in by **`prompt`** (used by dendrynexus). During startup, `winston.js` calls `common.setLevels(winston, …)` before `padLevels` is defined on `module.exports`, and Node warns when that property is read mid–circular require.

### Fix

In `node_modules/winston/lib/winston/common.js`, the check is now:

```javascript
if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(target, 'padLevels') && target.padLevels) {
```

instead of `if (target.padLevels)`.

`npm run dendrynexus make-html` no longer prints the warning.

### Persistence

- Added `scripts/patch-winston-padlevels.js` (idempotent).
- Added `"postinstall": "node scripts/patch-winston-padlevels.js"` in `package.json` so it runs after `npm install`.

Run **`npm install`** in the repo if you haven’t yet, so builds use **local** `node_modules/dendrynexus` (and the patched winston). A **global** `dendrynexus` install will still show the warning unless you patch that copy too or always use `npm run dendrynexus`.

Longer term, the same one-line change could go upstream in [dendrynexus](https://github.com/aucchen/dendrynexus) (bump/replace `prompt`, or vendor a patched winston).
